details.suggestions: The agent correctly retrieved the acetylene, co and hydrogen series for Transformer 1 at MAIN over the requested window (4 samples each), but then stopped without producing any anomaly results. It never ran tsfm.data_quality, tsfm.find_models (task_id tsfm_anomaly_detection) is not evidenced in the visible trace, and tsfm.run_recipe with task tsfm_anomaly_detection was never executed. The recipe_template output explicitly shows that an inline sktime_class detector (e.g. sktime.detection.lof.SubLOF) can be used without a catalog model_id, so the claim that 'the anomaly-model catalog returned no detectors' does not justify abandoning the task; the agent should have built a recipe with an inline detector and materialized the series into a dataset_path for run_recipe. Per-channel flagged timestamps, values and n_anomalies, the cross-gas timestamp check, and the escalation logic (acetylene+hydrogen -> immediate resample, co only -> routine retest, none -> stable) were all left 'Not determined', so the user received no actionable answer. At minimum the agent should have attempted the detector path, and if it truly could not run, provided tsfm.profile_series statistics (min/max/mean) with the 50%-above-mean rule as a clearly labeled provisional fallback rather than returning an empty table.

task_choices: omitted / anything else  - FORECASTING: transforms -> single|ensemble -> conformal
tsfm_anomaly_detection   - detector path, producing dense anomaly labels
estimator_spec: model_id     - a catalog card, e.g. {"model_id": "ttm_r1_512_96"}; its sktime_class and params are read from the card (see find_models / resolve_model)
sktime_class - an inline class path + params, e.g. {"sktime_class": "sktime.forecasting.naive.NaiveForecaster", "params": {"strategy": "drift"}}
optional_blocks: transforms - list of transform specs applied to the target before the forecaster
ensemble   - {"members": [<estimator spec>, ...], "combine": "mean|median|min|max|weighted|stack", "weights": [...]} - use INSTEAD of estimator
finetune   - training block; see param_hints (lr, epochs, batch_size, ...)
save_to    - directory path; after a fine-tune, persist the fitted weights there and return checkpoint_path in the result (feed it to register_finetuned)
eval       - {"metrics": ["smape", ...]} - the first metric scores the backtest
rules: a recipe MUST carry an `estimator` or an `ensemble` (not both)
`model_id` must exist in the catalog; run_recipe errors if it does not
run_tabular_recipe extracts FLOps features first, then fits `estimator`; omit label_column for clustering
the series itself is never in the recipe - it arrives via dataset_path
